title: Exercise 7B · Q3
summary: The corner-to-corner swim is the diagonal of the pool.
alt: Exercise 7B · Q3: A rectangular swimming pool has a length of 50 m and a breadth of 30 m. During a swimming proficiency test, Ethan has to swim from one corner of the pool to the opposite corner. Find the distance Ethan has to swim.

hyp.label: Hypotenuse
hyp.text: The side opposite the right angle. It is always the longest side.

legA.label: Shorter side 1
legA.text: One of the two sides that meet at the right angle.

legB.label: Shorter side 2
legB.text: The other side that meets at the right angle.

steps.title: The question
steps.narration: A rectangular swimming **pool PQRS** has a length of **50 m** and a breadth of **30 m**. Ethan swims from corner **P** to the opposite corner **R**. Find the distance Ethan has to swim.

steps.title: Spot the right angle
steps.narration: In ΔPQR, **∠Q = 90°**, so the **hypotenuse** is the side opposite it: **the swim distance PR**. The other two sides meet at the right angle.

steps.title: Pythagoras' theorem
steps.narration: **Pythagoras' theorem**: the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{PR^2} &= \role{legA}{PQ^2} + \role{legB}{QR^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Substitute the lengths
steps.narration: Replace each side by its length.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{PR^2} &= \role{legA}{PQ^2} + \role{legB}{QR^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{50^2} + \role{legB}{30^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Square and add
steps.narration: Square each number, then add them.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{PR^2} &= \role{legA}{PQ^2} + \role{legB}{QR^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{50^2} + \role{legB}{30^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{2500} + \role{legB}{900} \\ &= \role{hyp}{3400}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Square root
steps.narration: 3400 is not a perfect square, so use a calculator and round to 3 significant figures.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{PR^2} &= \role{legA}{PQ^2} + \role{legB}{QR^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{50^2} + \role{legB}{30^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{2500} + \role{legB}{900} \\ &= \role{hyp}{3400} \\ \role{hyp}{PR} &= \sqrt{3400} = \role{ans}{58.3\ \text{m}}\end{aligned}\]

formulas.title: Pythagoras' theorem
formulas.text: In a right-angled triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.

formulas.title: Finding the hypotenuse
formulas.text: Add the two squares, then take the square root.

formulas.title: Finding a shorter side
formulas.text: Subtract the known shorter side's square from the hypotenuse's square, then take the square root.

challenges.title: Now you try
challenges.prompt: A right-angled triangle has shorter sides **8 m** and **6 m**. Find the **hypotenuse**.

takeaways: Find the **right angle** first — the side opposite it is the **hypotenuse**.
To find the hypotenuse: **add** the squares of the two shorter sides, then take the **square root**.
The hypotenuse is always the **longest** side, so check that your answer is bigger than both of the other sides.

notes.title: Exam tip
notes.text: Always begin with a line such as "In ΔABC, ∠C = 90°. Using Pythagoras' Theorem," — it shows which triangle and which right angle you are using.

notes.title: Rounding
notes.text: If the answer is not a whole number, give it to **3 significant figures** unless the question says otherwise.
